subject.title: feat: expose ClawHub catalog feed lanes

question: Should ClawHub expose these root catalog feed lanes now, and if so must they use the existing stored-publication delivery and a distinct reviewed/official trust contract before merge?
rationale: The PR creates a new public API and client trust surface; automation cannot decide whether maintainers want dynamic root feeds, reviewed-lane semantics, or feed-id compatibility changes.

options.title: Require Snapshot-Backed Root Feeds
options.body: Update the PR to serve root lanes from `catalogFeedPublications` or an equivalent cached publication path, use distinct feed ids, regenerate contracts, and add live endpoint proof.

options.title: Approve Dynamic Root Feeds
options.body: Maintainers explicitly accept the request-time query model and reviewed/attestation semantics, then require docs and proof to match that chosen contract.

options.title: Pause The Feed Stack
options.body: Keep the draft paused or close it until the cross-repository feed RFC and OpenClaw consumer contract are ready to anchor ClawHub producer behavior.

recommendation.title: Require Snapshot-Backed Root Feeds
recommendation.body: Update the PR to serve root lanes from `catalogFeedPublications` or an equivalent cached publication path, use distinct feed ids, regenerate contracts, and add live endpoint proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen has recent history on the feed schema/spec contract that frames the public delivery and trust decision.
